quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #6
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: To see vehicles in your blind spots, you should check:

options.text: The inside rearview mirror.
The outside rearview mirror.
Over your shoulders.

questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Look over your shoulders to check them.

questions.question: It is unlawful to:

options.text: Pass another vehicle in any marked no passing zone.
Pass another vehicle over a railroad crossing.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: Do not pass in no passing zones or at railroad crossings. Also, do not pass on hills, in curves, at street crossings, when a vehicle has stopped for a pedestrian, or in work zones.

questions.question: In which situation should your wheels NOT point straight ahead?

options.text: When waiting to make a left turn at a traffic light.
When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.
When parked on the side of a level roadway where there is no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.
questions.explanation: On a hill, turn your wheels so your vehicle will not roll into traffic if the brakes fail. When waiting to turn left, keep wheels straight ahead so you do not veer into oncoming traffic if hit from behind.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Be ready to merge with traffic entering your lane.
Always stop.
Divided highway ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to merge with traffic entering your lane.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black markings. This sign warns that traffic will merge into your lane from the right. Be ready to let them merge safely.

questions.question: To pass on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn as you pass.
Flash your headlights as you pass.
Judge the distance to any oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judge the distance to any oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast oncoming vehicles are moving. Always make sure you have enough space to pass safely. If you are unsure, wait until the oncoming vehicle passes before you pass.

questions.question: If you want to pass a pedestrian and an oncoming vehicle is approaching, you should:

options.text: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.
Keep driving at a steady speed. The oncoming vehicle must stop for you.
Honk your horn to get the pedestrian to move over.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time. Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass. Then pass the pedestrian when it is safe.

questions.question: A sign with this shape means:

options.text: Railroad crossing.
Warning.
Signal ahead.

questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped yellow signs warn of danger ahead. Orange diamond signs warn of dangers in or near work areas.

questions.question: Sudden wind gusts on highways:

options.text: Generally affect only the movement of large vehicles.
Only cause visibility problems.
Can cause problems for all vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause problems for all vehicles.
questions.explanation: Strong wind affects all drivers, not just large vehicles. Wind can reduce visibility and physically move any vehicle.

questions.question: If you encounter an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Challenge them.
Get out of their way.
Speed up.

questions.explanation: The safest choice is to get out of the aggressive driver's way. Avoid competing with other drivers.

questions.question: When may you legally drive around or under a railroad crossing gate?

options.text: Never.
When you can see clearly in both directions.
When the warning lights are not flashing.

questions.explanation: Never go around or under a lowered gate. Once the gate is raised, wait until you can see clearly in both directions and are sure no trains are coming before you cross.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red traffic light, what should you do?

options.text: You are driving the wrong way.
Treat it like a stop sign.
Do not go until the light turns green.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. Come to a complete stop at the stop line or before the crosswalk. Yield to all other vehicles and pedestrians before proceeding.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when your tires slide on water instead of the road. How can you prevent it in wet weather?

options.text: Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Drive slower.
Move to the road shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Slow down when the pavement is wet to prevent your tires from sliding.

questions.question: When a school bus is picking up or dropping off children, you must:

options.text: Stop no matter which direction you are going.
Stop only if you are going the same direction as the bus.
Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop no matter which direction you are going.
questions.explanation: You must stop completely before reaching a school bus that is picking up or dropping off children, no matter which direction you are traveling.

questions.question: When you see a yellow school crossing sign, what should you do?

options.text: Always stop at the crosswalk.
Stop at the crosswalk until a crossing guard tells you to go.
Be ready to stop if children are in the crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if children are in the crosswalk.
questions.explanation: This sign means you are near a school. Watch for children and stop if they are crossing.

questions.question: When double solid yellow lines separate lanes of traffic, what does this mean?

options.text: You can pass from the left.
You can pass from the right.
You cannot pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean traffic is moving in opposite directions. You cannot pass other vehicles from either direction.

questions.question: You are leaving the interstate. When should you start slowing down?

options.text: Halfway through the deceleration lane.
As you get close to the deceleration lane.
Right when you enter the deceleration lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right when you enter the deceleration lane.
questions.explanation: Stay at your current speed until you enter the deceleration lane. Then slow down to match the posted speed for the exit ramp.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
Change lanes suddenly without warning.
Check for vehicles in the lane you want to enter.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and blind spots for other vehicles. Always signal before you change lanes to warn other drivers.

questions.question: When you see someone crossing the street with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Stop until they are safely away from your vehicle.
Honk and drive past them.
Drive carefully around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until they are safely away from your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stop completely for any pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog. These tools show the person is blind. Give them the right-of-way.

questions.question: When driving in fog, rain, or snow, use:

options.text: Low beams.
High beams.
Fog lights only.

questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, rain, and snow. High beams reflect off water and create glare that makes it hard to see.

questions.question: Before entering an intersection, you should look:

options.text: Left, right, then left again.
Right only.
Left only.

questions.explanation: Look left, then right, then left again before entering an intersection. Check for vehicles and pedestrians. Look a second time to the left because vehicles from that direction will be closer to you.

questions.question: How do stopping distances and crash severity change with vehicle speed?

options.text: They decrease as speed increases.
They are not affected by speed.
They increase as speed increases.

questions.explanation: Higher speeds mean longer stopping distances and more severe crashes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Stop sign ahead.
Divided highway.

questions.explanation: This sign tells you that turning right is not allowed.

questions.question: Why should you check your rearview mirrors?

options.text: Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.
To see if a vehicle is in your blind spot.
Only when you are slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirrors frequently so you know where vehicles are around you. Do not stare in one direction.

questions.question: How much lane width are motorcycles entitled to?

options.text: The bicycle lane.
Half the width of a lane.
The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have the right to use the full width of a lane, just like all other vehicles.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights behind you on a city street. What should you do?

options.text: Drive to the right edge of the road and slow down.
Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.
Stay in your lane, slow down, and let it pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Move to the right edge and stop for any emergency vehicle using its siren and lights. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then stop.

questions.question: What are "No zones" around trucks?

options.text: Areas where cars disappear into blind spots or are too close for the truck driver to stop and maneuver safely.
Areas where cars have enough space to travel behind the truck.
Areas where cars have several car lengths between them and the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas where cars disappear into blind spots or are too close for the truck driver to stop and maneuver safely.
questions.explanation: "No zones" are blind spots around trucks where cars cannot be seen or are too close. Cars in these areas greatly increase the risk of a crash.

questions.question: When a blind pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane crosses the street, what must you do?

options.text: Always yield the right-of-way.
Tell them where to cross the street.
Only yield the right-of-way at a corner.

questions.explanation: You must always give the right-of-way to any pedestrian using a guide dog or carrying a white cane.

questions.question: Which of these is a safe driving technique?

options.text: Using your high beam lights in fog.
Staring at the road ahead of your vehicle.
Checking your rearview mirrors frequently.

questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirrors every two to five seconds to stay aware. Do not stare at just the road ahead. In fog, use low beam headlights, not high beams.

questions.question: What does this sign tell you?

options.text: A construction flagger is ahead.
A police officer is ahead.
A parking attendant is ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that a flagger is ahead. Always follow the flagger's directions. Flaggers wear bright orange, yellow, or yellow-green clothing and use paddles or red flags to direct traffic through construction zones.

questions.question: When must you stop your vehicle?

options.text: At any intersection when a police officer orders you to stop.
At a red traffic light.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: You must stop at a red traffic light. You must also obey any orders given by a police officer directing traffic, even if signs or signals say otherwise.

questions.question: Water on the road can cause hydroplaning. Your car may hydroplane at speeds as low as:

options.text: 45 miles per hour.
35 miles per hour.
40 miles per hour.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when there is standing water on the road. At 35 mph or slower, most tires can push water away from the tire. At speeds above 35 mph, tires cannot push water away as well. Your tires may lose contact with the road and slide over the water like water skis.

questions.question: Use your headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days:

options.text: To keep your engine warm.
So others can see your vehicle.
To warn others of bad weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: So others can see your vehicle.
questions.explanation: On rainy, snowy, or foggy days, other drivers have trouble seeing your vehicle. Headlights make your vehicle easier to see. If you need to use your windshield wipers, you must also use your low beam headlights.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle, it is safe to return to your driving lane when:

options.text: The driver you passed signals for you to return to your lane.
You signal your intention for three seconds.
You see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before returning to your driving lane, make sure you are far enough ahead of the vehicle you passed. Look in your inside rearview mirror. When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your mirror, you have enough room to return to your lane.

questions.question: An orange and red triangular sign on a vehicle always means:

options.text: The vehicle has the right-of-way.
Slow-moving vehicle.
Shoulder work ahead.

questions.explanation: Slow-moving vehicles display an orange and red triangle on the back. These include farm tractors, road maintenance vehicles, and animal-drawn carts.

questions.question: The speed limit in school zones is:

options.text: 20 mph.
30 mph.
45 mph.

questions.explanation: In school zones, you cannot drive faster than 20 mph unless a different speed limit is posted. Always drive carefully near children.

questions.question: A driver should:

options.text: Assume all drivers automatically obey the right-of-way rules.
Assume most drivers obey the right-of-way rules.
Always be prepared to yield the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be prepared to yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Right-of-way rules help guide drivers, but no one should assume they have the right-of-way. Always look at the situation at an intersection. Be ready to give up your right-of-way if it helps prevent a crash.

questions.question: Before switching on the ignition, you should:

options.text: Buckle your safety belt.
Be sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: Create a routine when getting in and out of your car. Before starting the engine, buckle your safety belt and make sure all passengers do the same.

questions.question: If you come to a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing warning lights, you should:

options.text: Drive around the crossing gates if you can't see a train.
Come to a complete stop well behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, and proceed once the gates are lifted.
Slow down and drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop well behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, and proceed once the gates are lifted.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when signs, warning devices, or flaggers tell you a train is coming. It is illegal to drive around lowered gates.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No passing zone.
Slow-moving vehicle.
Two-way traffic.

questions.explanation: A yellow triangular sign with black lettering means no passing zone. It appears on the left side of a two-way, two-lane road where you cannot pass other vehicles.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Use your high beam headlights.
Use your parking lights.
Use your low beam headlights.

questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in fog. High beams reflect off the fog and make it harder to see.

questions.question: Why should drivers give extra space to children on bicycles?

options.text: Children do not react as quickly as adults.
Children are smaller and harder to see.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: Children are unpredictable and hard to see. Watch carefully for children near schools, bus stops, playgrounds, parks, and ice cream trucks. Children on bikes may ride onto the road without warning.

questions.question: When driving behind a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Be ready to use your horn.
Drive more slowly.
Keep a larger distance between your vehicle and the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a larger distance between your vehicle and the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Stay at least 3 to 4 seconds behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop quickly. If the rider falls, you need extra space to avoid hitting them. Wet roads, gravel, and metal surfaces like bridges increase the risk of falls.

questions.question: A steady green light means:

options.text: Speed up.
Adjust your mirrors.
You may go through the intersection at a safe speed if it is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may go through the intersection at a safe speed if it is clear.
questions.explanation: A green light means you can proceed through the intersection. Yield to any traffic or pedestrians already in the intersection. Only go when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: This sign warns you that:

options.text: No turns are allowed.
The road is narrowing.
There are curves ahead.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to hazards ahead. This sign warns of a winding road with curves.

questions.question: As you enter a roundabout, slow down and:

options.text: Yield to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing.
Yield to cars already in the roundabout.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and any vehicles already inside.

questions.question: When approaching a curve, slow down:

options.text: Before you enter the curve.
After you finish the curve.
In the middle of the curve.

questions.explanation: Reduce speed before entering a curve. Driving too fast can cause your tires to slip off the road.

questions.question: After a train passes at a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Wait until the warning lights stop flashing.
Check for a second train.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: After a train passes, watch for a second train on another track. Do not go until all gates are up and all warning lights have stopped flashing.

questions.question: A U-turn is not allowed:

options.text: In a parking lot.
On or near curves or hills.
On a straight road where you can see 500 feet ahead in both directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: On or near curves or hills.
questions.explanation: Never make a U-turn on or near a curve or hill. You cannot see oncoming traffic or pedestrians and may cause a crash.

questions.question: When turning left at a corner, yield to:

options.text: Other vehicles turning left.
All oncoming vehicles.
Pedestrians waiting for the walk signal.

questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and all vehicles moving on their green light.

questions.question: If heavy smoke covers the road ahead, you should:

options.text: Turn on your flashers and keep going.
Slow down, move right, and stop off the road.
Turn on high beams and continue.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move right, and stop off the road.
questions.explanation: If you see heavy smoke ahead, slow down immediately, move as far right as possible, and stop off the road. Then check if it is safe to continue. Some smoke can harm your eyes, lungs, or health.
